SURGICAL WOUND CLASSIFICATION AND ANTIMICROBIAL PROPHYLAXIS RECOMMENDATIONS

# >>  Clean  <<

A wound resulting from a procedure in which no inflammation or infection was encountered and the respiratory, alimentary, genital, or uninfected urinary tract was not entered.  Clean wounds are closed at the end of surgery and if drainage is necessary wounds are closed with drains in place.

Antimicrobial prophylaxis is usually not indicated.  Exceptions are procedures in which prosthetic material will be inserted or for operations in which a surgical site infection would be catastrophic.  These exceptions include most cardiac operations, joint replacement, revascularization procedures in legs, and most neurosurgical operations.

# >>  Clean contaminated  <<

Clean-contaminated wounds are those in which the respiratory, alimentary, genital, or urinary tracts are entered but there is no evidence of infection and there is no major break in technique.  These include operations on the biliary tract, appendix, vagina, and oropharynx.

Antimicrobial prophylaxis is indicated for most of these procedures.

# >>  Contaminated  <<

Contaminated wounds include an open, fresh, accidental wound, or operations with major breaks in sterile technique, gross spillage from the gastrointestinal tract, or incisions in which acute, non-purulent inflammation is encountered.

Antimicrobials are therapeutic and not prophylactic.

# >>  Dirty-Infected  <<

Dirty-infected wounds are old traumatic wounds with devitalized tissue and those that involve existing infection or perforated viscera.  The organisms usually have been present in the operative field since before the operation.

Antimicrobials are therapeutic and not prophylactic.
